hero.lead: I build software from the interface down to the system it runs on. I like the part where it has to actually work.

about.label: About
about.title: I like turning things that don't work into things that do.
paragraphs: Usually that means software. Something is unclear, slow, or broken, and I want to understand it before I start changing it.
I like the whole path, not only the framework in front of me. The screen someone uses, the API behind it, and the machine it runs on are one problem.
Away from the computer I am often in the workshop, taking something mechanical apart, or playing drums. I like both. They are a good reminder that not every problem lives in a text editor.

bluenordix-lead.summary: I lead development and still build with the team. The day-to-day is technical direction, architecture, and quality: keeping the codebase and the systems maintainable, rather than managing from a distance.

bluenordix-apprentice.summary: My apprenticeship, on production software with a small team. I worked across the stack and took on significant parts of the product. It was hands-on development during vocational training, not a stretch of ordinary full-time employment.

pcv-data.summary: I led the team as Scrum Master and kept a hand in the code. A shorter, full-time role, mostly about how a team builds software together.

personal-portfolio.name: Personal Portfolio
personal-portfolio.summary: A portfolio website that is also a software project — designed and built from scratch.
personal-portfolio.imageAlt: The portfolio homepage, with the name Kevin Møller Madsen and two actions.
personal-portfolio.sourceNote: The source is public on GitHub, for anyone who wants to see how the portfolio is built.
overview: This is my personal portfolio. I designed and built it as a custom Angular application, with a Laravel backend, in a monorepo.
It presents my work, experience, skills, and background. It is also a software project in its own right: the same one you are looking at.
I did not want an online CV and nothing else. The portfolio is a chance to show how I approach a product: the interface, the structure, and the problems along the way.

role.detail: I designed and built the interface, from the page structure to the type and the feature components.
Laravel lives in the same repository. I run it locally with DDEV. The pages do not call it yet.
The layout reads typed data through one service, so the pages are not tied to the files that hold the content today.

paragraphs: The repository has two applications side by side. Frontend/ is the Angular site. Backend/ is Laravel.
Feature components read that service. It is the place an API can take over later.
architecture.diagram:
portfolio/
├── Frontend/    Angular application
└── Backend/     Laravel application

decisions.title: Laravel and DDEV
decisions.body: The backend is PHP, developed locally with DDEV.

decisions.title: One repository
decisions.body: Frontend and Backend sit next to each other.

decisions.title: A portfolio service
decisions.body: Templates read the service. The copy and the records sit behind it, not inside the layout.

decisions.title: Fluid layout
decisions.body: Type and spacing grow with the screen, then stop, so a large display does not turn the page into a billboard.

decisions.title: A quiet interface
decisions.body: Near-black, with deep navy in it. Motion is an entrance and a hover, then it stops.

challenges.problem: The page had to stay comfortable on a phone, fit a 1080p display, and still not look like a narrow column on a much larger screen.
challenges.approach: Sizes are fluid up to a point, and the reading column has a maximum width. Past that, the page stops growing.

challenges.problem: The first navigation highlight followed how much of a section was on screen. A tall section could stay active after the reader had moved on.
challenges.approach: The active item is now the last section that has passed a line just under the header.

result: The site is what I use to present the work. Building it is part of what it demonstrates.
This page is the template for the other projects, once they are written up.
